extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy voting members, artists/publicists/marketers submitting For Your Consideration (FYC) materials and hosting/promoting FYC events
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing how Recording Academy Voting Members must vote and how artists/publicists/marketers may solicit votes or promote GRAMMY-eligible recordings (FYC). Covers prohibited/promoted behaviors, allowed/disallowed FYC communications, event/gifting restrictions, third-party vendor rules, and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote only in your Fields and categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Only select and vote in the Fields and categories in which they work, day to day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting Members are entrusted to limit their voting to the areas where they have professional expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote based solely on artistic and technical merits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cast their votes based solely on the artistic and technical merits of eligible product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not base votes on sales, popularity, or non-artistic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voter Code of Conduct — avoid external influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not allow their choices to be suggested, directed or influenced by anything other than their own analysis of merit, including, but not limited to: personal friendships, company loyalties, regional preferences or sales volume/popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must perform independent merit-based analysis and avoid conflicts of interest or biased group pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No accepting money or things of value for votes or privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not accept money or anything of value in exchange for votes, access to other members (member lists and contact information are confidential), submission of materials for GRAMMY consideration, or any other privilege of Recording Academy membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any quid-pro-quo or value exchange tied to voting or access is strictly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No agreements or understandings on how to vote (no voting blocs/vote trading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voters shall not enter into any agreements or understandings on how to vote. This includes without limitation: 'Voting Blocs' ... or 'Vote Trading.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizing groups of voters to vote together or trading votes is forbidden. Examples given include label-affiliated blocs or social-media-linked groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy corrective action and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If any activity is determined to work in opposition to the Recording Academy’s guidelines, the Academy may take any corrective actions, including disqualification of entries. Members who authorized or enabled solicitation that undermines the rules may be subject to suspension or termination of membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations can lead to entry disqualification and membership sanctions; Academy/independent accountants may take confidential corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final voting confidentiality and independent tabulation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the announcement of nominations, the final ballot is made available to all current Voting Members ... All ballots ... are tabulated confidentially by an independent accounting firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final results are kept confidential until awards day; results are delivered sealed by the independent firm (Deloitte).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescindment policy — no replacement award
rubrics_metrics.description: In any situation where a GRAMMY Award is withdrawn following the presentation, no award is given in that Category for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The GRAMMY process does not produce ranked runner-up results; rescindment does not produce an alternate winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC proprietary information restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers specific to an official Awards Category, Field and/or balloting, entry lists and finals lists are proprietary information belonging to the Recording Academy; such information may not be used, disclosed, published, or otherwise distributed in connection with any event, advertisement, or for any other purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Academy internal lists or balloting numbers in promotional materials or events.

rubrics_metrics.name: FYC communications must include opt-out
rubrics_metrics.description: For Your Consideration (FYC) marketing communications ... are prohibited unless they include an opt-out option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All emails, mailings, invitations, social media, websites, print ads used for FYC must include a clear way for recipients to opt out of future communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion limited to one’s own recordings; no lobbying for others
rubrics_metrics.description: Members or their designated publicists are restricted to promoting only their own recordings. There shall be no lobbying on behalf of other members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicists/members cannot promote third-party recordings or solicit votes on behalf of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy member contact information confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Be advised that the Recording Academy does not release the contact information of its members, therefore you should exercise caution if doing business with any vendor claiming that the vendor has accurate contact lists of Academy members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors claiming access to member lists are not legitimate; reliance on such vendors can result in disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed FYC communications content
rubrics_metrics.description: FYC Communications can include the following: Artwork related to product under consideration; Brief, unembellished descriptions of the recording or creators; Copies or links to product; Links to websites that promote eligible recordings; Link to Recording Academy website where Voting and Solicitation Guidelines are posted; Lists of the creators who worked on the recording; Reference to nominations, once nominations are announced. List Category(s) by full name; Reference to the GRAMMY Award with proper registered marks (reference can be made by name only; use of logo is prohibited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain factual information and provided wording rules when referring to nominations and GRAMMY marks; do not use logos (logo use reserved for paid sponsors/partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content in FYC communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications CANNOT: Cast a negative or derogatory light on a competing recording; Exaggerate or overstate the merits of the music, an achievement or an individual; Include any Recording Academy trademarks, logos or any other protected information; Include entry list numbers or Category numbers; Include chart numbers, number of streams, sales figures, or RIAA awards; Include personal signatures, personal regards or personal pleas to listen to the eligible recordings; Misrepresent honors or awards, past or present; Reference the year or the telecast number (i.e., 2022 or 65th GRAMMY Awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid comparative or promotional hyperbole, quantitative sales metrics, personal appeals, misuse of Academy intellectual property, or references to specific telecast years/numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark and logo usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to the GRAMMY Award with proper registered marks. Use of logo is prohibited, see below: GRAMMY®; GRAMMY® Award; GRAMMY Awards® (Only the plural GRAMMY Awards gets the ® on Awards.); GRAMMYs®
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If referencing GRAMMY marks, follow the exact approved word forms above; do not use Academy logos unless you are a paid sponsor/partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billboard GRAMMY Issues mailing and advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording Academy members receive a complimentary copy of Billboard GRAMMY Issues ... The Recording Academy does not disclose member contact information to Billboard. Any member can take out an advertisement in Billboard GRAMMY Issues. Advertising restrictions listed above apply. Special rates exist for independent creators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising in Billboard must follow the same FYC communication restrictions; members may opt out of receiving the magazine via their account subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting independent FYC events — no value exchange/hospitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent FYC events, programs, or activities may be hosted if they adhere to the guidelines ... FYC activities may not include any complimentary meals, alcoholic beverages, gifts, or any other hospitality that could be inferred as a value in exchange for vote consideration. Anything considered by the Recording Academy, in its sole discretion, as unreasonable promotion or gifting is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events must avoid providing perceived value to influence voting (no comps, freebies, or gifts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticketing for FYC events — no comps or discounts
rubrics_metrics.description: If members are invited to a ticketed FYC event or program, they must purchase tickets at full price (no comps or discounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts cannot comp or discount tickets for voting members as part of solicitation efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on gifting show tickets
rubrics_metrics.description: Widespread gifting of show tickets to members as part of an explicit or implicit FYC/vote solicitation campaign is not allowed. Recording Academy Chapters may not be used as a conduit for gifting ... Tickets that are not acquired by members through their own personal affiliations must be purchased at full price (no comps or discounts) — this includes tickets to films and musical theater productions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual, incidental ticket access through personal affiliations is acceptable; organized or broadly provided gifted tickets are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academy office mailings prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Any mailing of FYC product or marketing materials to any of the Recording Academy offices is prohibited, and will not be distributed to members, Governors or Trustees. Such mailings will be disposed of or returned to sender, in the Recording Academy’s sole discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send promotional materials to Academy offices; such items will be discarded or returned and may trigger penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone lobbying prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting Academy members by phone to promote a GRAMMY-eligible product or achievement is prohibited, even if such contact is in the guise of checking to make sure a sample product or other product was received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No phone solicitation or promotional calls to members regarding eligible recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party solicitation and vendor rules
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several marketing companies that claim to have authorized access to Recording Academy member lists and/or Recording Academy staff. There are no such businesses. If a vendor has obtained, through wrongful conduct, an accurate member list, we will disqualify any entry that used the vendor’s services. Additionally, marketing companies may not use subscriber-based publications to distribute promotional materials to an Academy member unless the member is a subscriber to those publications. The Academy defines 'subscriber' as a member who has taken the intentional step of requesting that a publication be sent to him or her on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not engage vendors claiming member-list access; using such services risks disqualification. Ensure any publisher-based distributions are to legitimate subscribers only. Review Recording Academy intellectual property regulations when engaging vendors.

rubrics_metrics.name: RecordingAcademy.com FYC feature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For Your Consideration promotional listings are available on RecordingAcademy.com free of cost ... The duration for the feature is the first round voting period. ... These entries may only be posted once in each of the approved FYC categories ... Duplicate posts ... miscategorized entries ... and promoting entries outside of the For Your Consideration groups are considered violations of these guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Academy's free FYC listing appropriately: post only once per approved category (allowed once in each accepted category), avoid duplicates/miscategorization, and do not promote outside approved groups; violations will result in removal and possible penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Recording Academy–hosted member-facing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: GRAMMY-submitted product cannot be the topic of any Recording Academy voting member-facing activity, event, or communication, including membership emails. Anyone who has submitted product for awards consideration during the then-current voting cycle can be featured by the Recording Academy at voting member-facing events or activities, as long as their submitted product is not the focus of the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submitter appears in Academy programming, their submitted work must not be the focal point; distribution of FYC product at Academy-hosted events is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting suspected violations
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage our community to help us monitor violations of these guidelines and ask that you report any findings to: 877-637-6816 / awards@grammy.com. It should not be assumed that any tactics or activities not specifically addressed by these regulations are acceptable. The Recording Academy is willing to review any materials or answer any questions that arise in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members and the public should report suspected violations using the provided phone/email; when in doubt, seek Academy review in advance rather than assuming permissibility.
